newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Kuwait Oil Company set to be awarded $600 mln.
newsitem.headline: Kuwait Oil Company set to be awarded $600 mln.

text.p: Kuwait Oil Company (KOC) has been recommended to receive some $600 million in damages for oil well fires set by departing Iraqi troops at the end of the Gulf War, Western diplomats said on Monday.
The recommended award, made by a panel of neutral judges named by the U.N. Compensation Commission, was expected to be approved later in the day by the body's Governing Council, they added.
Kuwait Oil Company set to be awarded $600 million =2

But the judges deferred action on $350 million of the total $951 million claim brought by KOC, saying it should be considered under another claim category, according to diplomats who asked not to be named.

The Governing Council, composed of the same 15 members of the Security Council, was meeting behind closed doors on Monday to take action on the KOC claim -- the first corporate claim processed by the Geneva-based war reparations body.

"About $600 million has been recommended by the panel of commissioners (judges). They deferred $350 million to go under a different claim and they also rejected a small amount," one Western diplomat told Reuters.
"Our view is that it should go through. It is widely anticipated that the Governing Council will approve the recommendation of the panel," he added.
